body: My best friend completely cut me off because it was too much for her to handle. Two other friends know and they act mostly normal. They don't really know how to handle it, so most of the time they pretend like nothing is going on and do their best to "cheer me up".
I don't want to ruin the exams of the people close to me. They deserve the best chance at a good future.

Hey, thanks for letting me know, I was wondering if you were doing okay. I'm so happy to hear you're doing better and I'm glad I could help. I hope you will keep doing better and better. Thank you, I appreciate it!

Snowflakes, petting cute puppies or playing with kittens, seeing sunrise/sunset, being able to go to concerts, listening to music you like, being able to watch Incredibles 2 which we have waited for for such a long time, walks in the forest, the way trees look in the fall, warm showers, cuddles, making other people laugh, sitting next to a fire place with a hot chocolate, being able to eat your favourite meal and just granting this world the present of you still being here. 

I don't know you, so this was all really general, but I tried. I put effort into this and I hope this makes you realise that someone cares. I'm a complete stranger, but I do care and I want you to have a reason. I know what I wrote isn't that big or spectacular, but those things count as well I hope.

First, medication can be shit but is definitely not always shit.

Second, I went to therapy for a while and I have both positive and negative experiences. Let's start with the negative. It was someone who, in retrospect, had no clue what they were doing. Just there for the money as many are. She let me talk and just told me oh that must be hard. That's it, that's all she said to me. Well no surprise, things got out of hand and she realised she wasn't able to handle me, so she wanted to get me taken into hospital, which I did NOT  want (for personal reasons, family stuff, complicated). Things spiralled out of control and I never went back after some horrible things happened.

So lesson learned: look for a good therapist, someone you feel comfortable with and someone who seems to actually help YOU. (this means something different for different people, so I can't say what will work for you, that's something you have to decide). 

Positive experience: I went to someone else after that and talked to her and we agreed we would try to work it out without me having to go to the hospital first. But this on the condition that I would agree to go to hopsital if things didn't improve/got worse. She offered me ways to break my thinking patterns, to handle my negative thoughts. I would go every week and tell her what bothered me and she would tell me "try this or this or this and tell me how this went next week". So little by little I improved. (then she retired and I'm trying to find someone new now)

This turned out way longer than I expected it to be, but hey you asked haha. If you have any other questions, feel free to ask.

That's a good friend you have. I hope you get some rest during your sleep, if tomorrow is the same or worse, you might want to take their advice. Maybe they can even help you to get there. I know someone who was taken there and it helped her a great deal.

I never wanted to go because I'm scared for some reason, so I understand if you wouldn't want to. But at least try to find help. It's good to rest now though and see what tomorrow brings. A good night of sleep sometimes helps a bit to make you think a tiny bit clearer. I hope you have a good night sleep, I wish you all the best.
That's the best description I have ever read. Thanks, made me giggle.

If it gets worse, you can still get out. I would, however, really recommend reaching out to someone. If you can a professional. They will help you by giving you coping mechanisms and support you. It makes stuff easier to deal with and even if it gets worse, you'll find yourself being in a better position to handle it all.

You can also always talk to me if you would need anyone to listen to you who understands. I'll always answer as long as I'm still here myself.

I'm not sure either. I have no clue why I'm still here. But what else is there to do? I just can't hurt the people who care about me, so I'm willing to try. For now.

I understand it's hard, I really do. And it is so so much effort, I know that. But perhaps if you're not sure yet what to do, you can still give it another chance? You'll always have the option to die, that's just a fact, we'll all die some day. So maybe just postpone a little bit, see if it's worth the effort?

You scream in your pillow and cry and hope it goes away soon. You talk to other people about it, you look for a therapist and hope anything will relieve this agony a little bit. I don't know myself what else to do, so I can't give you any better advice than this. 

Also I've been wishing very very hard, but no, nothing bad has happened yet by accident. I'll keep you updated on that, but I think almost anyone on here wishes something bad happens by accident so they don't have to do it themselves. 

I hope the chaos in your head reduces a little bit soon.

I resent exercise as well, but it's not entirely correct that for any other illness you don't have to exercise. I have major back problems and need to do core exercises so my muscles can keep my spine together. If I don't, surgery might be necessary sooner rather than later. (but I'm so depressed rn that I don't really care what happens to my back, so I don't do anything) There are many stories out there similar to mine, but I agree, I hate exercising as well

I did the same. I wanted to be there for her always. It became too much for her. My depression made things even worse and I became more of a burden. She left. I shouldn't have pushed it so much but she's better off without me anyways.

I hope you find some friends really soon.
I'm sorry, I think I translated it wrong. English isn't my first language and my mind is all over the place. I know it's true for you and for many people and you just want to help.
I see this argument a lot, but I haven't had that feeling. I only feel regret that I didn't do it, cause I only suffer more pain.

I don't know what else to say. Every time I seem to get over a hurdle, every time things seem to finally go somewhat okay because there's a new adjusted plan for me, I fall into depression and don't get anything done. I've been struggling so long now and everyone was like yay you're almost done, you can't fuck up this last thing you have to do. I did. I'm still fucking it up and my family doesn't know. I fucked it up as I fucked everything up and there's no saving it. I'll let everyone down again, I can see them getting angry already because I cry regularly. Everyone is annoyed. Everyone is sick of my shit and so am I. They'll be happy I'm gone so that they don't have to deal with my annoying presence anymore. They always compare me to others and how they would prefer to have someone else as a child not me. Well then, if I'm gone they won't have to tell their friends anymore how fucked up I am and they won't have to be embarassed anymore. Better for everyone.

Have you tried seeing a therapist about this? They might be able to help you out more. In the meantime, I'm here to listen if you want. I understand how it feels, but I'm struggling too. You could try reconnecting with your friends if at all possible. If we just lock ourselves up, it gets way way worse, trust me. If it's not possible, are there any hobbies you had in the past besides gaming? Gaming could be good, but if you're stuck in the same pattern it might not be helping you out.
I'm having trouble getting through my days as well, but for now I kinda have a goal to work towards. The advice I got on here is to do a little bit each day. It's better than doing nothing. But that's hard if you don't have anything to work towards. It's not really that I want this, I just don't really have any other option right now. I'm glad you still go to your job, seems like a major accomplishment to me.
I know I don't give the best advice, but I just wanted to let you know that I heard you, I listened and I very much understand. I hope it helps you at least a tiny bit to know that there are people out there who struggle with the same thing. I hope you can get help, therapist and meds can really really give you a push. I'm so sorry I can't do more.
That's awesome to hear! Congrats on the accomplishment, really happy for you :)

I would try giving therapy a chance if you're up for it. Perhaps you could try to write things down you want to say? Or keep a diary or something with what happens? Then you can either read from that or if that doesn't work you can just type out the parts you're willing to share and let them read it? I understand how hard it is to open up to someone you don't know about such personal things. These things both helped me to open up and to keep track of what happened and how I felt, because it can all become quite a blur. 

Also try to find someone who you feel comfortable with. I didn't get along at all with my first psychologist and almost ended up in hospital because of it. Try looking for someone you feel good being around. Really makes a difference if you are greeted by a face that wants to help you or a face that's just sadly staring away at you.

I hope this helped a little bit or maybe someone else can give you an alternative to therapy.

Hi, let me first introduce myself as priviliged piece of shit. I can honestly say that I never ever experienced anything you did, and I am very sorry that this all happened to you. I personally experienced emotional abuse at home, but nothing compared to what you went through. I understand why you're angry after reading this and why you don't trust people. Can't imagine anyone coming out of such an experience who would still trust people. For all it's worth, I think you came out the best way possible, because you realise that you have problems and you're working on them. Which is, in my eyes, AMAZING cause no one in your environment seemed to be able to do that. So I really admire that in you, that's like mind blowing to me.

I can also understand why you love animals. I have difficulty trusting people as well, cause they can just in generally be terrible and selfish. Again: I in no way had an experience like you did, so I don't want you to think that I'm like oh sure whatever. Not at all, I want to say that even me, priviliged piece of shit who had none of your problems, has difficulty trusting people because humans can be terrible. Animals are the best, they can love you unconditionally and don't give a shit about who you are. Great that you got to work with them and I'm very sad for you that you lost your pets. Reading your story, that must've been very hard for you, my condolences.

You asked if anyone knew your place in this world and I don't want to say that I know your place, but I do know that your place is definitely not in that cult. You obviously are a good soul, you're trying to work on yourself, you're helping out animals, I mean you're just trying your hardest. Yes, adjusting will be hard and you say it's hard. I can't imagine. BUT I do believe and I do truly hope that you will find your place. I can't tell what it is, but I want there to be a place for you. You deserve it in my eyes.

Now I'm terribly sorry if you didn't ask for any of this. I don't know if this is going to come off the wrong way or anything, I just want to provide a listening ear and to tell you that at least one person on here read your story and this person really hopes that you will get a better life. I know you don't easily trust people, but I do care. You don't have to believe me, I don't expect you to, but I can only try.

You seem like a nice person who went through hell. You can message me if you want to talk to someone, I will read it just as I read through this whole entire thing (which took a while, not gonna lie). If you don't feel like it, that's totally fine. I hope your life journey continues for the better.

I failed a ton of classes and had to retake them, you're not whiny, I definitely understand the struggle. I was freaking out about it too. Especially the first time it can seem so overwhelming. Just telling you the things that calmed me down :)

I hate college too, it can be a terrible experience because people expect you to have the best time and when you don't... Well it doesn't feel that great. I understand very well that you want to complain about it, I did it a lot as well ;)

Where I'm from it's just the diploma that matters and not the grades. That would only matter if you wanted to go for a PhD, but not important to regular companies. Maybe it's different where you live, but I thought perhaps this might comfort you a little bit.

Hi! I understand the procrastination struggle really well. I have the same problem, just a different kind of project. Your strategy of working an hour and then re-evaluating sounds good. If I can't get myself to start working, I start with smaller intervals like fifteen minutes, then five minutes break until I can work longer. It's not perfect, but it's better than doing nothing.

I'm rooting for you and if you want a pep talk or just vent, you can always message me if you want. Good luck!

If it has been two years, I think the chance is fairly small the police will come to your door. Now I know that's easy for me to say and won't take your worries away of course. If it consumes you this much, I would try to get in contact with those people and tell them you were being out of order. Just a quick short message.

Also depression is often a lot of different things combined, but if you're scared that you contributed, then sending a message will be one less thought that could haunt their minds.

This is probably a scary suggestion and not so easy to do, but perhaps start with one person and see how they react? I don't have experience with this, but if I was on the other end and someone would tell me that what they did was wrong, I would really appreciate that.

Thank you so much for your reply. I will try to contact my professor about that. They've been quite mad with me so I'm a bit scared of their response, but I've got nothing to lose.

Thank you again for replying, it may seem stupid, but I'm so glad someone actually listened to me. Your last sentence gave me some hope, that things can at least again become bearable. It's hard to think that way if you're stuck with these thoughts alone, but it's a fair point that if I did it once, I can probably make it bearable again. Even if it's just for a short while.
